exposure.name: REGISTRANT_SUBJECT_TO_A_LEGAL_MATTER
exposure.why: The registrant (or a party it names) is subject to, involved in, party to or a defendant in a legal matter.

exposure.name: REGISTRANT_IS_A_PARTY
exposure.why: A matter 'in which it was a plaintiff'; 'matters in which we are a defendant'.

exposure.name: ACCRUAL
exposure.why: An accrual the registrant makes; the adjudicated rule CLAIMS_ACCRUAL_IS_DISCLOSURE (self-insured claims, a litigation accrual review).

exposure.name: RECORDED_LIABILITY_CHARGE_OR_BENEFIT
exposure.why: An amount the registrant records: a benefit from stockholder litigation, a liability for claims.

exposure.name: SELF_INSURED
exposure.why: Self-insurance for the registrant's own claims.

exposure.name: A_MATTER_IN_A_COURT
exposure.why: The vocabulary of a specific proceeding: a filing, a court, an allegation, a ruling, a party. 'judgments' alone is not here: an accounting estimate is 'based on complex judgments'.

exposure.name: SETTLEMENT_OF_A_LEGAL_MATTER
exposure.why: A settlement of a legal matter. Settlements with taxing authorities are not one (a tax-position paragraph).

why_this_file: D02's Item 8 keyword (catalog/r6/text_business_candidates_v1.json, pattern 'legal') admits a paragraph wherever the word occurs. Readers judged 20 of the 85 admissions they read NOT_DISCLOSURE, and every one of them names litigation only as one item of a list or as an example in a parenthetical, in a paragraph that says nothing about a legal matter of the registrant: a list of cost categories, of matters counsel advises on, of risks that move estimates, of covenant add-backs, of what a tax audit can include, a collection policy '(including litigation, where appropriate)'. A paragraph leaves the set only when both hold. Business phrases live here rather than in executable code (tools/check_vnext_semantics.py); the file's bytes are recorded by the issue_47_v1 snapshot as a rule file, so a change here moves the Requirement closure.
